# Alloq implementation

Alloq is a Reflex 0.10 app for resource and project planning. The generic skills
explain Python, Reflex and appkit in general. This skill is the Alloq layer: where
code goes in this repo, which guards it must keep green, and how Alloq tests look.
When the two disagree, this skill wins, because it describes the code as it is.

Stack: Python 3.14, uv workspace (`UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT=.venv.mac`), Reflex 0.10,
appkit-* (`appkit_mantine as mn`, `appkit_commons`, `appkit_user`, `appkit_ui`),
SQLAlchemy 2.0 async, Pydantic, Alembic, PostgreSQL in production and SQLite in tests.
UI text is German. Code, comments and log messages are English.

## Workflow for every task

1. **Search memory** for the feature words and for error text you see. Past sessions
   stored traps here (for example the mixin rule and the umlaut escaping in tests).
2. **Read the reference code of the layer you touch** before writing. The canonical
   slice is departments (see the architecture map). Copying its shape is faster and
   keeps reviews short.
3. **Plan the smallest diff.** Change the layers the task needs and nothing else. Do
   not move files, rename folders or refactor neighbours unless asked.
4. **Write or adjust the test first**, in the test file of the package you change.
   For a bug, first write a test that fails because of the bug. Run the touched test
   files once before changing code, so you know which failures were already there;
   report those instead of fixing them inside the same diff.
5. **Implement.**
6. **Run the gates**: `task format && task lint && task typecheck && task test`.
   For a quick loop run only the touched test files with
   `uv run pytest <file> -q`, but run `tests/test_handler_authorization.py` whenever
   you add or change an event handler.
7. **Check file sizes**: `python .claude/skills/alloq-implementation/scripts/check_file_sizes.py`.
8. **Update memory** with any new trap or decision that the code itself does not show.

## Architecture map

Host app `app/` (entry `app/app.py`, admin pages `app/pages/*.py`, sidebar in
`app/components/sidebar.py`) plus uv workspace packages in `components/`:

| Package | Holds |
| --- | --- |
| `alloq-commons` | shared kernel: entities, models, repositories, shared services, shared UI, `theme.py`, `roles.py`, `access.py` |
| `alloq-project` | projects and planning: `components/`, `services/`, `states/`, `pages.py` |
| `alloq-dashboard` | dashboard and portfolio: same layout, `models.py` for card payloads |
| `alloq-team` | team overview and employees: same layout |

Layers, in the order data flows (paths for departments under
`components/alloq-commons/src/alloq_commons/`):

| Layer | Where | Rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Entity | `entities/department.py` | `class XEntity(Entity, Base)`, `to_dict()` with every field |
| Model | `models/department.py` | Pydantic read model plus `XCreate` write model with `Field` limits |
| Repository | `repositories/department_repository.py` | `BaseRepository[XEntity, AsyncSession]`, `model_class`, module singleton `x_repo` |
| Service | `<pkg>/services/*.py` | pure functions and dataclasses; DB loading kept in `*_inputs.py` or loader functions |
| State | `state/department_states.py` | `rx.State`, `rx.Field` vars, `@rx.event` handlers |
| Component | `components/department.py` | plain functions returning `rx.Component`, built from `mn.*` and shared parts |
| Page | `app/pages/departments.py` or `<pkg>/pages.py` | page factory `create_x_page(sidebar, route, title)` using `app_page` |
| Registration | `app/app.py` | call the factory with `sidebar()`; add a sidebar entry if needed |
| Migration | `alembic/versions/YYYY_MM_DD_<topic>.py` | hand-written, real `downgrade()` |

Dependency direction: feature packages import `alloq_commons` and appkit, never
`app` (`tests/test_component_boundaries.py` fails otherwise). Feature packages do not
import each other unless that import already exists. `app` may import everything.

`alloq_commons` has both `state/` (departments, roles) and `states/` (holidays). Put
new code next to its closest neighbour and do not merge the folders unasked.

Details, snippets and the background-load pattern: `references/architecture.md`.

## Where does this code belong?

- **Pure calculation** (scores, sums, sorting, grouping, labels) goes into a service
  function or a small dataclass, testable without a database. Examples:
  `alloq_dashboard/services/resource_path.py`, `alloq_project/services/project_sorting.py`.
- **Database reads and writes** go through a repository method, or a loader function
  such as `load_departments()` or `portfolio_inputs.py`. States do not build SQL.
- **UI state** (open dialogs, filters, toggles, selection) lives in the state. When the
  state file is large, put new vars and handlers into a mixin
  (`class XListState(rx.State, mixin=True)`), never into a substate; substates break
  tests that create the state on its own.
- **Rendering** goes into function components that read state vars. No logic beyond
  `rx.cond` / `rx.foreach` and formatting.
- **A value both the UI and a test need** (labels, messages, column lists) becomes a
  module constant, so tests can assert on it.

## Security: the handler authorization contract

Access levels (`alloq_commons.access`): admins may do everything; the project
manager role may read and edit every planning page (dashboard, planning, projects,
team) but not the administration; the employee role may only read planning and
projects. Page guards (`admin_only=True`, `editor_only`, `viewer_only`) only hide
the page. Event handlers run over the websocket for anyone with a session, so every
handler protects itself. `tests/test_handler_authorization.py` enforces this for all
states in the four packages. For each new or changed handler pick exactly one case:

1. **Reads or writes data in a planning package** (`alloq_dashboard`,
   `alloq_project`, `alloq_team`, `SidebarState`) → `@rx.event` then
   `@requires_editor` from `alloq_commons.access`. This is the default; the guard
   test rejects `@requires_admin` there.
1b. **Administration state** (`DepartmentState`, `RoleState`, `HolidayState`,
   `DatabaseAccessState`, listed in `ADMIN_STATES`) → `@requires_admin` from
   `appkit_user.authentication.decorators`.
2. **Read-only load the employee role may also run** → `@requires_viewer` from
   `alloq_commons.access`, and add the name to `VIEWER_HANDLERS`. It must not write.
3. **Only changes UI state** (open/close, set filter, toggle) → no decorator, add the
   name to `UI_ONLY_HANDLERS["<ConcreteState>"]`. The test scans its source and the
   `self.` helpers it calls for DB markers (`get_asyncdb_session`, `_repo.`,
   `aggregation.`, ...), so a UI-only handler must not touch a repository or session.
4. **Background handler** (`@rx.event(background=True)`) → guard decorators are not
   allowed (they need the state lock). Check edit rights inside `async with self`
   through `_CardLoadMixin._run_card_load` (`_can_edit`) and list it in
   `INLINE_ADMIN_CHECK`.

Edit controls in the planning UI go inside `editor_only(...)` or use
`disabled=~CAN_EDIT`; `admin_only(...)` is for administration only.

Handlers defined in a mixin are listed under the concrete state that mixes it in
(`TeamState`, `ProjectState`, `PlanningStore`), because the test skips mixins.
Remove allowlist entries when you delete or guard a handler; stale entries fail too.
Run the test after every handler change.

## Style that ruff does not catch

- German UI strings, including toasts: `rx.toast.error("Fehler beim Erstellen der
  Abteilung.", position="top-right")`. English for code, comments, docstrings, logs.
- `logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)` per module; `%s` arguments, never f-strings
  in log calls; `logger.exception(...)` in the final `except Exception` of a handler.
- Handler error shape: `ValidationError` → German hint, `IntegrityError` → duplicate
  message, `Exception` → `logger.exception` plus a generic German error toast.
- Colors, radii and shadows only from `alloq_commons.theme` (`theme.CARD`,
  `theme.TEXT_MUTED`, `theme.BLUE[6]`, ...). The theme is macOS blue; ignore the old
  teal design artifact.
- Use `mn.*` components. Load `appkit-mantine-reference` before using one you have
  not used in this task; its props are not in your training data.
- HTML attributes on `mn` inputs: `max_length=20` turns into CSS and limits nothing.
  Use `custom_attrs={"maxLength": 20}` for the browser limit, and keep the real check
  in the write model (`Field(max_length=20)`).
- State vars: `name: rx.Field[T] = rx.field(default)`; lists use
  `rx.field(default_factory=list)`. Type hints on every function, including tests.
- Prefer shared parts over new ones: `modal_form_layout`, `modal_footer`,
  `delete_dialog`, `toolbar_search`, `primary_button`, `section`, `app_page`,
  `window_toolbar`, `de_number`.

## Testing standards

Coverage must stay at 80 % or more (branch coverage, `fail_under = 80`). Put tests in
the package that owns the code: `components/<pkg>/tests/test_<feature>.py`. App-level
tests and the guards live in `tests/`.

- **Entity/model**: `to_dict()` keys, `XCreate` rejects bad input.
- **Service**: plain unit tests with hand-built inputs, no mocks needed.
- **State**: create the state directly, patch `MODULE.x_repo` and
  `MODULE.get_asyncdb_session`, fake the admin with `_as_admin`, and drive handlers
  with `_run`, which returns the toast text. Copy the helpers from
  `components/alloq-commons/tests/test_departments.py`.
- **Component**: render with `str(component())` and assert on var names or module
  constants. `str()` escapes umlauts (`ä` becomes `\u00e4`), so assert on the constant.
- **Migration with data changes**: add a test in `tests/test_migrations.py` that runs
  the migration offline on SQLite.

Recipes and snippets: `references/testing.md`.

## Definition of done

- [ ] Test written first; new behaviour and the bug case are covered
- [ ] `task format && task lint && task typecheck && task test` all green
- [ ] `tests/test_handler_authorization.py` and `tests/test_component_boundaries.py` green
- [ ] Every new handler has its guard or its allowlist entry
- [ ] New migration is hand-written, uses `op.batch_alter_table` for column changes,
      has a real `downgrade()`, and its revision is added to `KNOWN_REVISIONS` in
      `app/desktop/schema.py`
- [ ] No touched file grew past 1000 lines; files already over it did not grow
      without reason (see `references/pitfalls.md`)
- [ ] German UI text, theme tokens, no `print`, no f-strings in logs
- [ ] Memory updated with new traps or decisions

Per change type (new field, new handler, new page, new service, bug fix):
`references/checklists.md`. Known traps: `references/pitfalls.md`.

## Which generic skill for what

| Need | Skill |
| --- | --- |
| Python style, logging, typing, design patterns | `python-coding`, `python-clean-code` |
| Reflex state design, events, background tasks | `reflex-state-and-architecture`, `reflex-docs` |
| Writing state tests in general | `reflex-testing-state` |
| Config, service registry, repositories, column types | `appkit-commons` |
| Any `mn.*` component or prop | `appkit-mantine-reference` |
| Shrinking a big file you touched | `code-cleanup` |

        """Run one edit; a toast comes back when it did not go through."""

        editor = MapEditor(get_asyncdb_session, offer_id, await current_user_name(self))

"""The story map as a grid of plain values for the page (from a map snapshot)."""

from typing import Any

NO_SLICE_ID = 0
NO_SLICE_TITLE = "Ohne Umsetzungsschnitt"
ORIGIN_SOURCE = "Quellenstellen"


def _card(story: dict, task_title: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    refs = len(story["source_refs"])
    return {
        "id": story["id"],
        "key": story["key"],
        "title": story["title"],
        "meta": f"{task_title} · {story['scope']} · {story['origin']}",
        "scope": story["scope"],
        "skeleton": story["skeleton"],
        "origin": story["origin"],
        "sentence": story["sentence"],
        "refs": f"{refs} {ORIGIN_SOURCE}" if refs else "ohne Quellenbezug",
    }


def build_view(snapshot: dict) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Columns, slice rows, option lists and a story lookup for the editor."""
    activities = [a for a in snapshot["activities"] if not a["archived"]]
    slices = snapshot["slices"]
    tasks_of = {
        a["id"]: [t for t in a["tasks"] if not t["archived"]] for a in activities
    }
    columns = [
        {
            "id": a["id"],
            "title": a["title"],
            "tasks": " · ".join(t["title"] for t in tasks_of[a["id"]]),
            "task_id": tasks_of[a["id"]][0]["id"] if tasks_of[a["id"]] else 0,
            "first": index == 0,
            "last": index == len(activities) - 1,
        }
        for index, a in enumerate(activities)
    ]

    def cell(activity: dict, slice_id: int) -> dict[str, Any]:
        stories = [
            _card(s, t["title"])
            for t in tasks_of[activity["id"]]
            for s in t["stories"]
            if not s["archived"] and (s["slice_id"] or NO_SLICE_ID) == slice_id
        ]
        first_task = (
            tasks_of[activity["id"]][0]["id"] if tasks_of[activity["id"]] else 0
        )
        return {
            "activity_id": activity["id"],
            "task_id": first_task,
            "stories": stories,
        }

    row_defs = [(s["id"], s["title"], True) for s in slices] + [
        (NO_SLICE_ID, NO_SLICE_TITLE, False)
    ]
    rows = [
        {
            "slice_id": slice_id,
            "title": title,
            "editable": editable,
            "cells": [cell(a, slice_id) for a in activities],
        }
        for slice_id, title, editable in row_defs
    ]
    lookup = {
        str(story["id"]): {
            **_card(story, task["title"]),
            "role": story["role"],
            "goal": story["goal"],
            "benefit": story["benefit"],
            "task_id": str(task["id"]),
            "slice_id": str(story["slice_id"] or NO_SLICE_ID),
        }
        for activity in activities
        for task in tasks_of[activity["id"]]
        for story in task["stories"]
        if not story["archived"]
    }
    return {
        "columns": columns,
        "rows": rows,
        "stories": lookup,
        "story_count": len(lookup),
        "task_options": [
            {"value": str(t["id"]), "label": f"{a['title']} · {t['title']}"}
            for a in activities
            for t in tasks_of[a["id"]]
        ],
        "slice_options": [{"value": str(NO_SLICE_ID), "label": NO_SLICE_TITLE}]
        + [{"value": str(s["id"]), "label": s["title"]} for s in slices],
    }

The Story Map now fills the pane like the planning grid, and it has the second bar with filters. The columns and story cards look the same as before. All tests, lint and typecheck pass, and I checked it in the running app on demo offer 5.

**Layout** ([map_view.py](components/alloq-offer/src/alloq_offer/workshop/components/map_view.py), [aq-workshop.css](assets/css/aq-workshop.css))
- No card, no padding and no rounded corners. The map fills the space below the toolbar and scrolls both ways inside it.
- The header with the activities stays at the top when you scroll down. It has the same grey background and thick bottom line as the planning header.
- The column with the slice names stays on the left when you scroll sideways, with the same right border as the planning grid.
- "Aktivität hinzufügen", "Umsetzungsschnitt hinzufügen" and the AI proposal request are now in a footer bar at the bottom, like the legend bar in planning. When a proposal is open, it shows as a strip just above the footer instead of as a card.

**Filter bar** ([workshop_view.py](components/alloq-offer/src/alloq_offer/workshop/components/workshop_view.py))
- It only appears on the Story Map tab once a map exists.
- It has a story search (by key and title), "Umfang" and "Umsetzungsschnitte" filters, a "Nur Skeleton" switch and "Filter zurücksetzen". The summary is on the right.
- The two dropdown filters work like the planning ones: once you pick something, the field shows a count such as "Umfang (1)".
- The slice filter hides whole rows. The other filters only hide story cards, so the "+ Story" buttons stay visible.
- The filtering is a plain function, `filter_rows`, in [services/map_view.py](components/alloq-offer/src/alloq_offer/workshop/services/map_view.py). The new setters on `MapState` only change what is shown, so I added them to the UI-only list in the handler authorization test.

def _title(value: str) -> str:
    title = value.strip()
    if not title:
        raise MapEditError(BLANK_TITLE)
    return title[:255]


async def _own[T: ActivityEntity | TaskEntity | StoryEntity | SliceEntity](
    session: AsyncSession, entity: type[T], offer_id: int, row_id: int
) -> T:
    row = await session.get(entity, row_id)
    if (
        row is None
        or row.offer_id != offer_id
        or getattr(row, "archived_at", None) is not None
    ):
        raise MapEditError(NOT_FOUND)
    return row


async def _next_position(
    session: AsyncSession,
    entity: type[ActivityEntity | TaskEntity | SliceEntity | StoryEntity],
    *where: object,
) -> int:
    highest = await session.scalar(select(func.max(entity.position)).where(*where))  # ty: ignore[invalid-argument-type]
    return (highest or 0) + 1


class MapEditor:
    """The edits of one person on the map of one offer; every call returns the new
    revision and fails with ``MapConflictError`` when the given one is stale."""

    def __init__(self, sessions: SessionFactory, offer_id: int, user: str) -> None:
        self._sessions = sessions
        self._offer_id = offer_id
        self._user = user

    def _edit(self, revision: int):  # noqa: ANN202
        return map_edit(self._sessions, self._offer_id, revision)

    # --- activities, tasks, slices ---------------------------------------------

    async def add_activity(self, revision: int, title: str) -> int:
        name = _title(title)
        async with self._edit(revision) as (session, workspace):
            position = await _next_position(
                session, ActivityEntity, ActivityEntity.offer_id == self._offer_id
            )
            activity = ActivityEntity(
                offer_id=self._offer_id, title=name, position=position
            )
            session.add(activity)
            await session.flush()
            session.add(
                TaskEntity(
                    offer_id=self._offer_id,
                    activity_id=activity.id,
                    title=DEFAULT_TASK,
                    position=1,
                )
            )
            return await record(session, workspace, self._user)

    async def rename_activity(self, revision: int, activity_id: int, title: str) -> int:
        name = _title(title)
        async with self._edit(revision) as (session, workspace):
            (
                await _own(session, ActivityEntity, self._offer_id, activity_id)
            ).title = name
            return await record(session, workspace, self._user)

    async def move_activity(self, revision: int, activity_id: int, step: int) -> int:
        """Swap an activity with its neighbour (``step`` is -1 or 1)."""
        async with self._edit(revision) as (session, workspace):
            rows = list(
                (
                    await session.scalars(
                        select(ActivityEntity)
                        .where(
                            ActivityEntity.offer_id == self._offer_id,
                            ActivityEntity.archived_at.is_(None),
                        )
                        .order_by(ActivityEntity.position, ActivityEntity.id)
                    )
                ).all()
            )

---
name: mantine-class-position-override
description: A plain CSS class on an mn.* component loses to Mantine's own rules (e.g. ActionIcon position relative); compound the selector
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

A class from assets/css (see [[layout-css-in-assets]]) set on `mn.action_icon(class_name=...)` did not get `position: absolute`: Mantine's ActionIcon root rule `position: relative` won (found 2026-10-24, story map edge plus buttons). Compounding the selector with the Mantine root class fixed it: `.aq-map-plus.mantine-ActionIcon-root { position: absolute; }`.

**Why:** Mantine's stylesheet loads after the app CSS with the same specificity.
**How to apply:** when a custom class on an mn component seems ignored, check the computed style first and add the `.mantine-<Component>-root` class to the selector rather than `!important`. In the same check, Playwright reported "Stack intercepts pointer events" for those absolutely placed buttons although `elementFromPoint` returned the button; a DOM `click()` opened the popover fine.

content.text:
You can now add activities and slices from plus buttons on the edges of the map. In the running app I checked that both popups open with the name field focused and that "Abbrechen" closes them. I did not press OK there, because the local profile writes to the shared database. The tests cover saving instead, and all gates pass.

**Columns (activities):** when you hover the header row, a small plus appears on every column edge. There is one on the right edge of the "Aktivität / Aufgabe" corner (inserts as the first column), one between each pair of columns, and one after the last column. Clicking it opens "Aktivität hinzufügen" with a name field and Abbrechen / OK. OK inserts the new activity exactly at that edge, Enter works too, and the popup closes. Escape, Abbrechen or a click outside closes it without saving.

**Slices:** when you hover a slice name in the first column, a plus appears on that row's top edge. It inserts a new slice right there, so the edge under the header puts it first and the edge above "Ohne Umsetzungsschnitt" puts it last. A slice filter does not change where a new slice lands.

What changed underneath:
- **Saving at a position:** `MapEditor.add_activity` and `add_slice` in [map_edit.py](components/alloq-offer/src/alloq_offer/workshop/services/map_edit.py) take an optional `index` and renumber the positions. Without an index they still add at the end. Archived activities are left out when counting the position.
- **Popup:** each column and row carries its `index` in the view, and `MapState` remembers which popup is open (`insert_at`). The two new handlers that open and close it are on the UI-only list in the authorization test.
- **Footer:** I removed the two "hinzufügen" fields from the footer, because the plus buttons replace them. The footer now only holds the AI proposal request.

In Playwright, a normal click on the column plus was blocked with an "intercepts pointer events" error. The browser itself reports the plus as the topmost element at that point, and opening it through the page worked. Still, try one click with a real mouse.

* all the "plus" buttons should be visible when hovering in the "Aktivität Aufgabe" col
* the plus buttons are moving when clicked (they seem not to have a fixed position)
* the layers seem not correct (see screenshot)
* the header row should drop the "anforderungen", the titel should be editable when hovering over it with the mouse
* the first col with the "stufen" should be smaler, only as wide that the "Ausbaustufe" (longer texts should be trimmed with a hover text)

content.text:
All five points are fixed. I checked them in the running app, and lint, typecheck and the 2195 tests pass.

- **Pluses show when you hover the first column:** hovering anywhere in that column, the corner included, now shows the plus on every row edge at once. Hovering the header row still shows all the column pluses.
- **Pluses no longer move:** Mantine nudges every button down by 1 px while it is pressed, and that wiped out the CSS I used to center the pluses, so they jumped. They are now placed with fixed offsets, and the press nudge is turned off for them.
- **Layers:** the bug in your screenshot came from lifting the hovered slice label above the header, so it covered the header while you scrolled. I removed that lift, so rows scroll under the header again. The plus above the first slice now sits on the bottom edge of the header corner instead of inside the first row, so it can't be hidden either.
- **Header row:** the "Anforderungen" line is gone. Titles look like plain text, and on hover they show a white field with a thin border, with a blue border while you edit. I also removed "Aufgabe" from the corner, because that row no longer exists, so the corner now says only "Aktivität".
- **First column:** it is now 150 px wide, which fits "Spätere Ausbaustufe". Longer names end in "…" and show the full name when you hover, for example "Ohne Umsetzungs…".

The width is set by `LABEL_COL_PX` in [map_state.py](components/alloq-offer/src/alloq_offer/workshop/states/map_state.py), and the plus and title styles are in [aq-workshop.css](assets/css/aq-workshop.css).

I could not test the click itself in the browser, so it would be good to check once with a real mouse that a plus stays still when you press it.

"""The story map as a list: one line per story, edited like a spreadsheet."""

from typing import Any

import reflex as rx
from alloq_commons import theme
from alloq_commons.components.excel_grid import (
    excel_grid,
    grid_cell_attrs,
    grid_row_attrs,
)
from reflex.vars import ObjectVar

import appkit_mantine as mn
from alloq_offer.workshop.states.map_state import MapState

LIST_LABEL = "Story-Liste"
DETAILS = "Details öffnen"
LIST_COLUMNS = (
    ("activity", "Aktivität", "minmax(140px, 1fr)", 0),
    ("title", "Story", "minmax(180px, 1.4fr)", 300),
    ("story", "User Story", "minmax(280px, 2.4fr)", 1000),
    ("description", "Beschreibung", "minmax(220px, 2fr)", 4000),
)
"""Column key, header, grid width and text limit (0: read only)."""
DETAILS_WIDTH = "44px"
TEMPLATE = " ".join(width for *_, width, _ in LIST_COLUMNS) + " " + DETAILS_WIDTH

Row = ObjectVar[dict[str, Any]]


def _cell(row: Row, column: str, limit: int) -> rx.Component:
    value = row[column].to(str)
    attrs = grid_cell_attrs(row["id"].to_string() + "|" + column, column, value)
    attrs.update(
        {
            "data-cell-type": "text",
            "data-read-only": "false" if limit else "true",
            "data-max-length": limit or 255,
            "title": value,
        }
    )
    return mn.box(
        value,
        custom_attrs=attrs,
        class_name="aq-list-cell",
        c=theme.TEXT if limit else theme.TEXT_MUTED,
    )


def _row(row: Row) -> rx.Component:
    return mn.box(
        *(_cell(row, column, limit) for column, _, _, limit in LIST_COLUMNS),
        mn.box(
            mn.action_icon(
                rx.icon("panel-right-open", size=15),
                variant="subtle",
                color="gray",
                size="sm",
                on_click=MapState.select_story(row["id"]),
                aria_label=DETAILS,
                custom_attrs={"title": DETAILS},
            ),
            class_name="aq-list-details",
        ),
        custom_attrs=grid_row_attrs(row["id"].to_string(), "stories"),
        class_name="aq-list-row",
        data_selected=MapState.selected_id == row["id"].to_string(),
        style={"gridTemplateColumns": TEMPLATE},
    )


def _header() -> rx.Component:
    return mn.box(
        *(
            mn.box(title, class_name="aq-list-head-cell")
            for _, title, _, _ in LIST_COLUMNS
        ),
        mn.box(class_name="aq-list-head-cell"),
        class_name="aq-list-head",
        custom_attrs={"data-grid-header": "true"},
        style={"gridTemplateColumns": TEMPLATE},
    )


def story_list() -> rx.Component:
    """Stories of the visible rows; title, sentence and description are editable."""
    return excel_grid(
        _header(),
        rx.foreach(MapState.list_rows, _row),
        id="story-list-grid",
        grid_label=LIST_LABEL,
        revision=MapState.revision,
        dirty=False,
        saving=False,
        navigation_guard=False,
        on_commit=MapState.apply_list_changes,
        on_reject=MapState.notify_rejected,
        class_name="aq-map-scroll aq-story-list",
        style={"outline": "none"},
    )

content.text:
All six points are done. Lint, typecheck and the 2205 tests pass. In the running app I checked the list, the inspector and opening a cell editor, but I cancelled with Escape, so no edit was saved.

There was no save button before: the inspector saved each field when you left it. It now saves only when you click the save icon or press Enter in a field. Closing the inspector or picking another story without saving loses your changes.

**List view** ([map_list.py](components/alloq-offer/src/alloq_offer/workshop/components/map_list.py))
- A "Map | Liste" switch sits at the start of the filter bar, and the filters work in both views.
- The columns are Aktivität (read only), Story, User Story and Beschreibung, sorted by activity, then slice, then map order. A button at the end of each row opens the inspector.
- It reuses the Excel-like grid from the planning grid and the price list: click to select, type or double-click to edit, arrow keys, copy and paste, fill, undo. Each batch of edits is saved as one map revision.
- You edit the User Story cell as a full sentence, "Als … möchte ich …, um …", and it is split back into role, goal and benefit. A cell that doesn't fit that form is not saved, and a warning toast says how many were skipped.

**Description**
- Stories have a new `description` field with up to 4000 characters. It shows in the list and as a multi-line field in the inspector.
- The migration is [2026_10_29_offer_story_description.py](alembic/versions/2026_10_29_offer_story_description.py). `alembic current` shows the shared database is already at this revision, so there is nothing to run.

**Inspector** ([story_drawer.py](components/alloq-offer/src/alloq_offer/workshop/components/story_drawer.py))
- The header with the story number and title stays at the top while the fields scroll.
- The title can be edited in place and shows a field frame on hover, like the map titles. I removed the separate "Titel" field.
- The top right has three icons, from left to right: save, archive and close (x). The old Archivieren and Schließen buttons at the bottom are gone; "Aufteilen" and the AI split button stay there.

    rows: list[dict[str, Any]],
    *,
    search: str = "",
    scopes: Collection[str] = (),
    slice_ids: Collection[str] = (),
    skeleton_only: bool = False,
) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Rows of the chosen slices with only the stories matching every filter."""
    needle = search.strip().casefold()

    def keep(story: dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
        text = f"{story['key']} {story['title']}".casefold()

INITIAL = "initial"


def is_initial(payload: dict) -> bool:

async def queue_initial_chapters(
    session: AsyncSession, offer_id: int, *, now: datetime, max_attempts: int
) -> JobEntity:
    """Stage ``chapters``: draft every prose chapter and keep it as revision."""
    return await enqueue_exclusive(
        session,
        kind=DRAFT_CHAPTERS_JOB,
        offer_id=offer_id,
        payload={"keys": None, "instruction": "", INITIAL: True},
        now=now,
        max_attempts=max_attempts,
    )


async def finish_initial_draft(
    session_factory: SessionFactory, offer_id: int, *, now: datetime, max_attempts: int
) -> None:
    """Stages ``checks`` and ``word_draft``: AI review and the first Word file.

    The export runs the rule checks on the state it fixes. A stage that cannot
    start is logged and skipped, so the chapters stay saved.

    try:

107:Der Nutzer erhält zuerst ein verständliches Bild der umzusetzenden Kundenprozesse und danach einen daraus abgeleiteten Angebotsentwurf. Er erkennt, welche Prozessschritte vom Kunden beschrieben wurden, welche als notwendige Ergänzung vorgeschlagen werden und wo fachliche Entscheidungen fehlen. 155:Mit offenen Punkten darf weitergearbeitet werden. Der Umgang mit kritischen Scope-Konflikten und kommerziellen Festlegungen bleibt ausdrücklich geregelt. Eine vollständige Einzelbestätigung aller extrahierten Sätze oder jedes Bearbeitungsschritts ist nicht erforderlich.

293:Die Map-Zuordnung, fachliche Herkunft und der Scope sind getrennte Dimensionen. ---
name: workshop-tests-real-clock
description: Workshop job handlers queue follow-up jobs with datetime.now(UTC); tests that claim jobs at a fixed NOW break once the real date passes NOW
metadata:
  type: project
---

`initial_draft` and other workshop jobs queue the next stage with `datetime.now(UTC)`, not the job's own `now`. `test_workshop_pipeline.py` claimed jobs at a fixed `NOW + 1 day` (NOW = 2026-10-24), so on 2026-10-25 the chapter stage was "not due" and the chain seemed to stop after `initial_draft`. Fixed 2026-10-25 by claiming at `datetime.now(UTC) + timedelta(days=1)`.

**Why:** looked like a regression from a feature change but was a date bomb.
**How to apply:** when a workshop pipeline or queue test suddenly stops after the first job, compare the test's fixed clock with today before debugging the code. See [[workshop-local-demo-ai]].

Fertig: Das „Umfang“-Feld ist komplett entfernt, die Zusammenfassung im Inspector ist weg, und die Spaltenköpfe haben das neue Layout. Lint (bis auf eine fremde Datei, siehe unten), Typecheck und alle 2200 Tests laufen durch. Im Browser konnte ich diese Runde nicht prüfen, weil die alloq-App gerade nicht läuft.

**Inspector**
- Der graue Kasten mit dem zusammengesetzten Satz ist weg. Der Hinweistext darunter bleibt.
- Das Feld „Umfang“ ist entfernt.

**„Umfang“ komplett entfernt**
- **Datenbank:** Die Spalte `offer_stories.scope` wird mit der Migration [2026_10_30_offer_story_scope_removed.py](alembic/versions/2026_10_30_offer_story_scope_removed.py) gelöscht. `alembic current` zeigt, dass die gemeinsame Datenbank schon auf diesem Stand ist. Es ist also nichts mehr auszuführen.
- **Code:** Entfernt sind die Umfangs-Werte, das Ändern des Umfangs, der Umfangs-Filter in der Filterleiste und „Umfang bestätigen“ samt Entscheidung und Zähler „Angeboten“ im Entwurf-Tab.
- **Neue Regel:** Jede nicht archivierte Story gehört zum Angebot. Wer eine Story nicht anbieten will, archiviert sie. Deshalb enthält schon der erste Word-Entwurf alle Stories, ohne Zusatz wie „(Angeboten)“.
- **Prüfung:** Die alte Prüfung „angebotene Stories fehlen“ meldet jetzt nur noch eine leere Story Map.
- **Alte Daten:** Gespeicherte Kapitel und frühere Word-Exporte, die noch einen Umfang enthalten, lassen sich weiter laden. Dafür gibt es einen eigenen Test.
- **Weitere Stellen:** KI-Prompts, Vorlage, Demo-Skript, Feature-Doku und Spezifikation sind angepasst. In der Spezifikation habe ich A25 auf „Vorschlagsherkunft bleibt sichtbar“ gekürzt.

"""Resizable grid columns, shared by ExcelGrid (``resize_key``) and plain grids.

A column's width is the CSS variable ``--grid-col-<key>`` on the grid root. Use
:func:`column_width` in the grid template, put :func:`resize_handle` into the
column's header cell (it must be positioned) and give the root a storage key:
``excel_grid(..., resize_key=...)`` or :func:`column_resize` for other grids.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any

import reflex as rx
from reflex.vars.base import Var

from alloq_commons import theme

_JSX_IMPORT = rx.asset("column_resize.jsx", shared=True).importable_path

RESIZE_HANDLE_CLASS = "grid-col-resize"
RESIZE_HINT = "Breite ziehen · Doppelklick setzt zurück"


class ColumnResize(rx.Component):
    """Plain div that owns the column width variables of the grid inside."""

    library = _JSX_IMPORT
    tag = "ColumnResize"

    storage_key: Var[str]
    """localStorage key under which this viewer's widths are kept."""


column_resize = ColumnResize.create


def column_width(key: Any, default_px: int) -> Any:
    """Grid track for a resizable column: its stored width or the default."""
    if isinstance(key, Var):
        return "var(--grid-col-" + key.to_string() + f", {default_px}px)"
    return f"var(--grid-col-{key}, {default_px}px)"


def resize_handle(key: Any) -> rx.Component:
    """Drag handle on the right edge of a header cell."""
    return rx.el.div(
        custom_attrs={"data-col-resize": key, "title": RESIZE_HINT},
        class_name=RESIZE_HANDLE_CLASS,
        style={
            "position": "absolute",
            "top": "0",
            "right": "-4px",
            "bottom": "0",
            "width": "8px",
            "zIndex": "4",
            "cursor": "col-resize",
            "touchAction": "none",
            "_hover": {
                "background": f"linear-gradient(to right, transparent 3px, "
                f"{theme.ACCENT} 3px, {theme.ACCENT} 5px, transparent 5px)",
            },
        },
    )
EOF

content.text: Alles grün. Ich speichere die zwei Fallen dieser Runde im Gedächtnis:

input.content:
---
name: reflex-shared-asset-folder-per-module
description: rx.asset(shared=True) copies into a folder named after the calling Python module; JS files that import each other must be registered from the same module
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

`rx.asset("x.jsx", shared=True)` places the file under `.web/public/external/<package path>/<calling module name>/`. On 2026-10-25 `column_resize.jsx` was registered from `excel_grid/column_resize.py`, so it landed in `.../excel_grid/column_resize/` while the helpers it imports (`column_resize.js`, `column_widths.js`) were registered from `excel_grid.py` and sat in `.../excel_grid/excel_grid/`. Vite failed with "Failed to resolve import ./column_resize.js" and the whole app showed "Application Error".

**Why:** the folder is per module, not per source directory.
**How to apply:** register every JS/JSX asset that imports a sibling from the same Python module (here `excel_grid.py` exposes `RESIZE_JSX_IMPORT`), and open the app after adding assets; unit tests do not catch this. Pure JS helpers stay in a React-free file so `node --test` can load them. See [[layout-css-in-assets]].

name: reflex-var-to-str-is-a-cast
description: In Reflex, var.to(str) only retypes the Var; comparing a str field with an int item needs .to_string() or the JS === is always false
metadata:

`MapState.selected_id == story["id"].to(str)` never matched: `selected_id` holds "12", the foreach item's `id` is the number 12, and `.to(str)` only changes the Python-side type, so the compiled JS compares `"12" === 12`. The selected story card never got its blue border (found 2026-10-25). `story["id"].to_string()` converts in JS and fixed it.

**Why:** Var `.to(T)` is a cast for typing, not a conversion.
**How to apply:** when comparing a string state field with a value from `rx.foreach` over dicts, use `.to_string()` on the item value; check such selection highlights in the browser (data attributes), since `str(component)` tests do not catch it.

content.text:
All four points are done and checked in the running app. Lint, typecheck, the 2220 Python tests and the 39 JS tests pass.

**Resizable columns, built into the Excel component**
Yes, it fits as a general feature. The resizing now lives once in `alloq_commons` (in [excel_grid/](components/alloq-commons/src/alloq_commons/components/excel_grid/)) and is used in two ways:
- **Excel grid:** `excel_grid(..., resize_key=...)` switches it on. The story list now has resizable columns this way, and the price list could get them the same way.
- **Other grids:** `column_resize(...)` is a thin wrapper for grids that are not Excel grids, like the story map with its cards.

For a resizable column you use `column_width(key, default)` in the grid template and put `resize_handle(key)` in its header cell. Each viewer's widths are saved in the browser per offer, and a double-click on the edge resets a column. In the app, dragging the first column took it from 230 to 350 px, the width was saved, and a double-click reset it.

**Slices as collapsible rows**
The narrow column on the left is gone. Each slice is now a full-width row like in planning: an arrow to collapse it, the editable name, and the story count ("5 Stories"). The left part stays in place when you scroll sideways. The plus buttons for new slices sit on the top edge of these rows, and the one for the first slice sits on the bottom edge of the header. A short gutter on the left keeps the plus before the first activity visible.

**Cards**
- Very light blue background.
- On hover a stronger blue and a clear drop shadow. The theme's normal card shadow was almost invisible, so I used its stronger window shadow.
- The selected story gets a 2 px blue border.

I found a bug along the way: the selected card was never highlighted, in the old version either. The selected ID (text) was compared with the card's number without converting it. That is fixed, and the browser now shows the blue border.

One more problem came up in the browser that the tests did not catch. Reflex puts shared JS files into a separate folder for each Python module, so a JSX file landed away from the files it imports and the whole app showed an error. All of those files are now registered from one module. I saved both traps to memory.

The columns now have their own widths and no longer stretch to fill the window. On a wide screen there may be empty space to the right of the last column. Nothing is committed yet.

* the plus should be left to the chevron
* in the header it should show up on the top left of a col header so that the resizer is not overlapping
* the cols should have a darker border color so that they are better visible in the board

---
name: reflex-form-in-foreach
description: An rx.form inside rx.foreach must not use the loop variable in on_submit; Reflex hoists handleSubmit out of the loop and the browser throws "<name>_rx_state_ is not defined"
metadata:

The story map edge popups (`_insert_edge` in `workshop/components/map_view.py`) used `on_submit=lambda form: handler(form, index)` with `index` from `rx.foreach`. Reflex compiles the form's submit into a separate `handleSubmit_…` function outside the loop, so clicking OK threw `ReferenceError: row_rx_state_ is not defined` and nothing reached the server (reported 2026-10-25). It only showed up once every popup lived inside a foreach.

**Fix used:** remember the context in state when the popup opens (`open_insert("activity:2")` → `insert_at`) and submit to a plain handler (`MapState.submit_insert`) that reads it.
**How to apply:** in `rx.form(..., on_submit=...)` inside `rx.foreach`, pass a bare event handler; put loop values into state on open/click (or into hidden inputs). `str(component)` tests do not show the hoisted handler, so click through such forms in the browser; an empty-name submit checks the round trip without writing data.

**Cause:** the popup form for the name sits inside the loop that draws the columns and slices. Reflex moves the submit function of such a form out of the loop. Our submit used the column or slice position from that loop, which no longer existed there, so the click failed in the browser and never reached the server. The bug was already there before; it only became visible once every plus moved inside the loop. The old corner plus used a fixed position and therefore still worked.

**Fix:** when the popup opens, the state already records which edge it belongs to (`insert_at`, for example "activity:2"). The form now sends only the name to a new handler, `submit_insert`, which takes kind and position from there. `add_activity` and `add_slice` use the same helper. Two new tests cover this, including the case where no popup is open.

**Not saved in the check:** I submitted both popups with an empty name, so nothing was written to the shared database. Adding stories quickly now works straight from the map. I tested it in the running app with a real story, and lint, typecheck and all 2225 tests pass.

- **Position:** the input sits at the bottom of each cell, so the inputs of a slice row line up on one line.

**App test:** I created "Testeintrag Schnellerfassung" in your test cell "Col2 / Test 2" and archived it again straight afterwards. The story key US-12 is used up by that, because keys are never given out twice.

This form also sits inside the loop that draws the cells, so task and slice are sent as hidden form fields. The handler `add_story` now takes the form and checks those values; a missing or invalid activity gives the familiar notice.
